newsitem.title: UK: London gold firms at fix aided by silver.
newsitem.headline: London gold firms at fix aided by silver.

text.p: Gold held near the top of its recent range on Friday supported by buying in silver and light short covering, but it looked vulnerable to a fresh tumble, dealers said.
"It's trying to go up but if there is no followthrough, I can see it coming off again," a dealer said.
Gold fixed at $355.75 per ounce after $354.10 this morning which was up $1.05 from Thursday afternoon. The market added around a dollar at the fixing to set a high bid of $355.90.
The February Comex contract was $1.50 firmer coming into the fixing at $356.50.
Dealers forecast that producer selling was likely if the price piked above $356.00
"If prices don't close tonight above $355 or $356, I think we could see more weakness," a dealer said. "There's no news, no incentive for anyone to buy gold."
The bottom end of the recent range has been the fresh 3-1/4 lows around $351.50 touched on Wednesday.
Important support levels were pegged at the psychological $350 area, $345 and then $330.

The fear of more central bank sales was still overhanging the market, while interest rates were muted, giving a further kick to galloping stock markets that have been regularly notching up fresh records.
Traders in Asia say physical gold demand has been fairly strong, with a shortage of kilo bars appearing in Hong Kong.
But London dealers said this would not be enough to stem the downward momentum. "Physical demand overall is steady but not huge," one said.
Writers of put options are not fully covered and any probing at new lows would spark delta hedging, accelerating any slide, option dealers said.
Silver was partially responsible for leading gold higher as it briefly pierced $4.80 just before the fixing.
"Silver has performed better than gold recently. It has held up relatively well and that has encouraged people to do a bit of buying," a dealer said.
However the market was divided on silver's upside potential, given the continuing gloom hanging over gold.
"I think it will have to move back to the $4.50s before it can really move higher," one dealer said.
Platinum was up about $1.25 at $360.50/$361.50 while palladium was around $0.50 firmer $121.25/$122.25.
